## Meeting
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, December 4, 2012, 5:45 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Agenda: pledge, recognition, closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), consent agenda, personnel, curriculum, business (2011-2012 audit), public communication, other, adjournment. Board roll: Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti. Meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and at vimeo.com/troyschools.

## Consent agenda and November 13, 2012 minutes
Consent items: minutes of the November 13, 2012 meeting and workshop, and the October 2012 Treasurer's Report. The attached November 13 minutes record Resolution 12-098 (consent, 7-0), Resolution 12-099 continuing summer tax collections under 1976 P.A. 451 for one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2013 (7-0), Resolution 12-100 claiming the Section 22f best practices incentive of $52 per pupil under MCL 388.1622f (roll call 7-0), Resolution 12-101 moving the December 4 start time to 5:45 p.m. (7-0), and Resolution 12-102 for closed session (7-0). Paula Fleming was recognized with an engraved rocking chair for completing her 12th year of Board service in June 2012.

## Personnel and reports
Probationary contracts recommended for Angela Locken (.5 FTE Great Start Readiness Preschool, Hill Elementary) and Sherry Richardson (first grade, Wattles Elementary). Jasen Witt reported on the Troy Educator Appraisal Model: overall ratings of 0% ineffective, 1% minimally effective, 96% effective and 3% highly effective, with the rubric cut from 75 elements to 53, a reduction of 30%.

## 2011-2012 audit
Teresa Pollock of Plante Moran presented for the year ended June 30, 2012: General Fund revenue $130,865,059 and expenditures 127,464,365, ending fund balance $23,078,581; debt service funds ended at $(1,859,077). Instructional expenditures were 66% for Troy against an Oakland County average of 61%. The Board was asked to accept the audited statements.

AGENDA. Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Closed Session on negotiations; Additions and Deletions; Public Communication; consent agenda of the November 13, 2012 meeting minutes, November 13, 2012 workshop minutes and the October 2012 Treasurer's Report; Personnel (Consideration: Elementary and Secondary; Report: Troy Educator Appraisal Model, TEAM); Curriculum; Business (Report and Consideration: 2011-2012 Audit); Public Communication on non-agenda items; Other; Adjournment. The closed session resolution cites the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with a roll call listing Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti.

MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 13, 2012. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. with all seven members present, two student representatives, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Colligan, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt, and approximately 10 audience members. Mrs. Paula Fleming was recognized and presented a specially engraved rocking chair for completing her 12th year of service on the Troy Board of Education in June 2012. Resolution 12-098 (moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mrs. Fleming) approved the minutes of the October 2, 2012 meeting, the October 16, 2012 workshop and the September 2012 Treasurer's Report, Yes 7 No 0. Resolution 12-099 (Edmunds/Schmidt, 7-0) continued summer tax collections for the 2013-2014 fiscal year; the attached Annual Summer Tax Resolution invokes, pursuant to 1976 P.A. 451 as amended, a summer levy of one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2013, directs that the request reach each city before January 1, 2013, and authorizes negotiation of reasonable collection expenses billable under MCLA 380.1612. Resolution 12-100 (Miletti/Underwood) accepted the Section 22f best practices incentive, a one-time grant of $52 per pupil for districts satisfying at least 7 of 8 criteria not later than June 1, 2013 under MCL 388.1622f, certifying medical-plan policy-holder status, competitive bidding of custodial, transportation and food services, non-resident enrollment under Section 105 or 105c (MCL 388.1705), a technology infrastructure plan filed with the Michigan Department of Education, postsecondary credit options under MCL 388.511 to 388.524, MCL 388.1901 to 388.1913 and MCL 380.1471, online instruction, and a home-page link to the MiSchool Data Portal; roll call passed 7 to 0. Resolution 12-101 (Underwood/Miletti, 7-0) moved the December 4, 2012 meeting to 5:45 p.m. in the Services Building. Mike Holz of Clinton Township addressed the Board on the district's 2008 playground equipment installation project and contract terms involving Outdoor Escapes, LLC and Landscape Architect Planners. Student representatives Aishawarya Singh (Athens) and Patty Durell (Troy High) reported. Mr. Schmidt noted the MASB Fall Conference at the Renaissance Center in Detroit and Troy Youth Assistance's Dollars for Education; Ms. Philippart noted an OCSBA dinner meeting on pending legislation. Resolution 12-102 (Edmunds/Fleming) approved a closed session for an attorney-client privilege item, carried 7-0; the Board entered closed session at 6:34 p.m., reconvened at 7:26 p.m. and adjourned at 7:27 p.m. Todd Miletti, Secretary. The November 13 workshop ran 7:35 p.m. to 10:40 p.m. on bond scope information (technology, buses, instructional equipment) and the bond communications plan.

PERSONNEL, ITEM 7.A. Probationary contracts for 2012-2013 recommended for Angela Locken, .5 FTE Great Start Readiness Preschool at Hill Elementary School, holding a B.A. in Early Childhood Education from Coastal Carolina University, Conway, South Carolina, December 2004, and a Michigan Provisional Certificate from August 2011, previously a special education para educator with Birmingham Public Schools; and Sherry Richardson, first grade at Wattles Elementary School, holding a B.S. in Elementary Education from Oakland University, Rochester, June 2010 and a Michigan Provisional Certificate from June 2010. Both reside in Troy, Michigan.

TEAM REPORT, ITEM 7.B. Presented by Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources, requiring no action. Drivers include revised school code 1249, effective September 2011, on rigorous standards for tenure and certification, and revised school code 1250 on compensation incorporating job performance. Annual evaluations are required for every teacher, with 700+ TSD teachers. The original and current TEAM committees each list 16 members, including Aaron Maliepaard, Brian Canfield, Tonia Romancheck, Mary Haezebrouck, Carrie Sekich, Jan Keeling, Karen Bush, Joe Duda, Anne Mull, Tim Fulcher, Stephen Lucchi (T.E.A. President) and Richard Machesky, with Harriet Clark, Nancy Lining and Danielle Szachta replacing Joe Brandinisio, Wendy Wilcox and Dina Chrisopoulos. Five domains cover planning and preparation, classroom environment, instruction, professional responsibilities and student growth. Overall ratings were ineffective 0 percent, minimally effective 1 percent, effective 96 percent and highly effective 3 percent. The rubric was scaled from 75 elements to 53, a reduction of 30 percent, with added rubrics for specialty areas such as media specialists and speech pathologists. Domain weights moved from 20 percent each in 2011-2012 to 15.0, 20.25, 24.75, 15.0 and 25 percent in 2012-2013. Rating bands moved from ineffective 25.0-55.0, minimally effective 55.1-67.0, effective 67.1-90.0 and highly effective 90.1-100.0 percent to 25.0-57.9, 58.0-73.9, 74.0-86.9 and 87.0-100.0 percent. Next steps include training evaluators in the Danielson Framework for Teaching via Teachscape and consideration of peer coaching and peer observation models.
